description: Hip to gable loft conversion with first floor rear extension, roof lights to front and gable window
decision_conditions: The proposed development, with reference to the hip-to-gable roof conversion, would alter the basic shape of the roof on the semi-detached dwelling which would be unacceptable as it would give rise to a visually heavy roof to one half of the semi-detached pair of properties, something which would have a negative effect on the street scene by creating a loss of symmetry between the two properties. Furthermore, the proposed rear dormer window extending over the existing rear extension / projection, by reason of its depth, bulk, scale, massing and materials, would appear as an unacceptably dominant and visually intrusive development in the rear garden scene which would be out of scale and character with the host dwelling and thereby materially harmful to visual amenity. The proposals would therefore be contrary to Local Plan Policies 7 and 26 and Policy D4 of the London Plan.

The proposed hip-to-gable roof conversion and rear dormer window, by reason of their combined bulk, scale, massing, depth and proximity to the flank kitchen window of no. 165 Warren Drive, would give rise to an intrusive and unneighbourly development that would have an adverse impact on the amenity of these adjoining occupiers through resulting in an overbearing impact, loss of outlook and appearing as a continuous wall of development from their kitchen window, contrary to Local Plan Policy 7 and the Residential Extensions and Alterations Supplementary Planning Document.

Statement Required by Article 35 (2) of the Town and Country Planning (Development Management Procedure) (England) Order 2015: Consideration was given to seeking amendments, but given conflict with adopted planning policy, notification of intended refusal and the reasons for it was given to the agent via email on 15/10/2026.

The Local Planning Authority has acted positively and proactively in determining this application by assessing the proposal against all material planning considerations, including planning policies and any representations which were received.  It subsequently determined to grant planning permission in accordance with the National Planning Policy requirement that applications for sustainable development are approved where possible.  A detailed analysis of the scheme is set out in the report on the application prepared by officers.
